headline: New evening confusion since about mid-October, including a stove left on (Nov 2), has no documented work-up results, and his primary caregiver reported exhaustion on Nov 22 and asked for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 the RN recorded that his grandson Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The plan was a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week.
items.verifier_note: The date, evening confusion for about two weeks, stove left on once, orientation, no fever and the plan are all in the note. The note does not say Robert is the grandson. That relationship appears only in the social work note, which this item does not cite.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22 the social worker met with Robert, the primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion and poor sleep, said he is worried about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. This overlaps with the period of evening confusion.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches every detail. The 2026-11-02 RN note supports the overlap with the evening confusion.

items.statement: The review period contains no urinalysis result, medication review or PCP visit addressing the confusion after 2026-11-02. No encounters are recorded, and the RN check on 2026-11-13 says only 'no new concerns'. Whether the planned work-up happened is not documented.
items.verifier_note: The encounters record is empty. The 2026-11-13 RN note says only 'No new concerns' and mentions no urinalysis, medication review or PCP visit. The statement correctly says the work-up is not documented.

items.statement: The 2026-09-25 fall note was corrected on 2026-09-27 as documented on the wrong participant, so it is not reported as a fall here. The PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 (TUG 19 seconds, walker and grab bar recommendations, twice-weekly PT) is written as following that fall. Whether it applies to Jerónimo is unclear and needs verification.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-09-27 correction says the 09-25 fall entry was on the wrong participant. The 09-29 PT evaluation follows that fall and contains the TUG of 19 seconds, the walker and grab bar recommendations, and twice-weekly PT. Flagging it for verification is appropriate.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-02 completed, and what were the results?
What evening safety measures are needed given the stove incident (e.g., stove safety, evening supervision)?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window, plus any since the last IDT review, to establish the period of change.

Falls and near-falls: check incident reports and nursing notes for falls, especially given osteoporosis on alendronic acid, scoliosis, and new antiplatelet/beta-blocker exposure; note any fracture, injury, or post-fall assessment.
ED visits and hospital admissions: review for any chest pain, cardiac events, or migraine-related ED use, given new ischemic heart disease diagnosis (2026-06-30) and chronic intractable migraine.

Cardiac status: review new ischemic heart disease follow-up, chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, heart rate and blood pressure trends on metoprolol, and any cardiology or primary care visits scheduled or completed.
Bleeding and antiplatelet safety: check clopidogrel-related bleeding signs, GI bleeding, bruising, or hematology labs; flag for team review without recommending changes.

Medication reconciliation: compare the five active medications (metoprolol succinate, alendronic acid, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) against the record for any starts, stops, dose changes, or missed doses in the window; confirm the simvastatin and alendronic acid start dates are consistent with the chart.

Substance use history: given dependent drug abuse (2018), review any opioid or controlled-substance prescriptions, early refill requests, pharmacy flags, urine drug screen results, relapse or treatment-engagement notes, and any changes to the pain regimen for chronic pain and migraine.
Chronic pain and migraine: review pain scores, migraine frequency and days lost, rescue medication use, and any new pain-management referrals or interventions during the window.

Osteoporosis care: check that bone density follow-up, calcium and vitamin D status, and dental/jaw considerations with alendronic acid (note impacted molars on problem list) are documented and due items are flagged.

Function, cognition, mood, and social: check ADL/IADL changes, weight trend (BMI 30+ history), cognition screens, depression or anxiety screening, IDT and social-work attendance, caregiver or housing changes, and care-plan items due before 2026-11-30; note that no allergies are recorded and verify that.
